title: A teaching test looks for worked ground instead of making some, and CI goes red when the map has none
tier_reason: It turns main red for a reason that is not a break, which is the one thing the CEO has said a red build must never mean.
ask:
tools/test_runner.gd, scenario AH (_scenario_ah_the_mark_one_takes_exact_orders), the 'one square, one tap' block. The lesson row is staged from x=13 to x=19 on row 11, and the search for a square to drag the finger across starts at x=20 and only accepts teachable ground. Nothing stages x=20 onward, so the assertion 'there is an unmarked square to drag over' passes only when the generated farm happens to leave worked ground there. CI run 35493586333 (f5b4afb, 2026-09-20) failed on exactly that while the same commit was green on every machine here.

Fix: stage the candidate before testing it, so the scenario says what it needs instead of hoping for it. Inside the existing loop, after `var cand := Vector2i(tx, lesson[0].y)`, add:

    _stage_tile(cand.x, cand.y, "seeded", "wheat")

and a comment saying why the square is worked here rather than looked for. Nothing else in the scenario changes; the rule under test ('a drag marks nothing') is untouched.

This was written on 2026-09-20 by a session that could not apply it, because another session was holding tools/test_runner.gd for the Q-110 (b) implementation at the time. Check whether it has already landed before doing anything.
first_action: Open tools/test_runner.gd and find `there is an unmarked square to drag over`; if the line above the loop body already calls _stage_tile, this is done and the card can be closed.
source_message: CI red on f5b4afb, 2026-09-20, while both suites were green locally.
